newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro-Council hits Russia, Ukraine on death penalty.
newsitem.headline: Euro-Council hits Russia, Ukraine on death penalty.

text.p: The Council of Europe's parliamentary assembly threatened on Wednesday to lock out delegates from Russia and Ukraine unless they quickly imposed a moratorium on capital punishment as promised.

An assembly resolution called on both countries to honour commitments to block future executions, as they had pledged when they joined the 40-nation council, which promotes democracy and human rights across Europe.
The assembly said there had been 89 executions in Ukraine and 53 in Russia during the first six months of 1996.

Russia, which joined the body in February 1996, and Ukraine, which did so in November 1995, both promised at the time they became members to impose immediately a moratorium on executions, and to abolish the death penalty within three years.

"We are fully conscious of the time needed to reach a complete abolition of the death penalty. That is why we are asking these two countries to immediately put in place a moratorium on executions in line with their commitments," deputy Renate Wohlwend of Liechtenstein said in a council statement.
"The abolition of the death penalty will take place in stages," Russian deputy Nickolay Fyodorov said during the assembly debate.
Council officials said some 15 of its 40 members including Belgium and Britain have not formally abolished the death penalty though they have imposed moratoriums on executions.
